URL: https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/vat-andy-burnham-cabinet-john-healey-government-b3018683.html
NOTE: Independent (21 Jul) — £850m VAT-on-electricity cut criticised as "unfunded." Helen Miller (director, Institute for Fiscal Studies): "disappointed" by policy that adds tax-system complexity and will be "hard to undo"; "Government think they have found funding for this year – but only by reallocating savings that haven't yet been made. If the Government can't add 5% VAT back onto bills next year, how will they pay for it next year and the year after?" Tory leader Kemi Badenoch: "It's only one day into Burnham's Government and already the explanations are falling apart. You can't use the funding from an unfunded programme to pay for cheaper bills." Martin Lewis (MoneySavingExpert): "a good totemic step and very welcomed" but "in practice people won't feel much benefit." VAT cut costs Exchequer ~£850m in 2026/27.
